RICHARD A. "DICK" GAY

Richard A. Gay, one of the earliest members of the faculty to be discussed, is among the most interesting to be included, if one is to judge by the number of sincere and affectionate references to him. His schoolmates say that he was known to all his friends and schoolmates as 'Dick' Gay, and came to Texas at the age of four from Georgia, with his family, and attended the public schools in Fannin County. When Savoy College opened he continued as a student there for a year or two, then went on to make his minister in 1880, at Ladonia, Fannin County. He conducted the Primary Department of the College as early as 1881-1882, and taught several years, all the while advanced work as a student in connection with his teaching.

For the years 1885-1886 he served in the State Normal College at Athens, Texas, where he was a member of the faculty and teacher of mathematics. During his latter days he recited from memory many times Tennyson's 'Crossing the Bar'—which at the close of his public life on earth was his wish—and that at the moment of his de-mise he preached the 11 o'clock service last at 891 Main St., Dallas, and then attended the night service. For by the time he was called to order by Judge Lindsey[?] Morrow, he could not hear. It was said he fell on the way to a prayer meeting when he could not hear. It was said he fell on the last day of March, 1887, the young doctor started out a successful career as a teacher.

He died of heart failure.²

${ }^{2}$Personal letter from Mrs. R. A. Gay, Paris, Texas, July 8, 1938.
